files.responsibility: Public entry of the kernel, `@svgframe/kernel` (design §3.10, P5a): the domain abstractions and extension-point interfaces that plugins may use.
The event buffer of one session (design §3.4).
Facade and Invoker (README §2.1, §2.7): one line of input in, its output lines out.

The session state behind one `Editor` (README §1.2): the current document (none until `init` / `read`), the default `save` path, the history, the event buffer, and the injected file system and committed extensions (design §2.2.5).
Cursor over the arguments of one command (the tokens after the command name).
Root of the command hierarchy (README §2.1).
The committed commands, read-only (design §2.2.5): what `help` and the parser need.
The four command groups of spec §3, in the order `help` lists them (V7).
What a command can see of the session (implemented by `EditorSession` in the app layer, and by a test double).
A resolved command line: the command type found by name plus its arguments.
One line of text → `CommandLine`: tokenize, then look the command name up in the registry.
Name dispatch #2 (spec §2.1): command name → command type.
The output lines of a successful command, warnings included.
The static side of a command class: the class object itself satisfies this interface, so `CommandRegistry` stores classes directly (README §2.5).
A document command (init, read, save, canvas with arguments).
An undoable shape-editing command (Template Method, README §2.6).
Undo and redo stacks of edit commands plus the io lock (spec §4.3, U1–U8).
Root of undo / redo: they act on the history inside `execute` and are not recorded themselves.
A read-only display command (tree, show, help, canvas without arguments): never recorded (U5).
One word of a command line.
Splits a command line into tokens at white space (convention R5):
What a command may do with the history (design §2.2.5): undo and redo, nothing else.

The four kinds of registration names a plugin declares under `contributes` (spec §6 loading contract): a closed set of value objects in the fixed order shapes → commands → decorators → attributes, the order in which duplicates are checked and manifest lists are written (design §3.3.1).
Subscriber to document events (design §3.4), registered with `PluginContext.subscribe`.

Every committed registration of one editor (design §3.3): the shape and command registries, the tree decorators, the attribute handlers, the document listeners, and the registration names per category in commit order.
The result of one `PluginInstaller.install`: success, or the single failure line (without the `error: ` prefix, which only the editor and the assembler add).
A plugin instance (design §3.1).
A plugin waiting to be installed (design §3.3.1, §4.1): how both ways of assembling an editor hand a plugin to `PluginInstaller`.
The shape of a plugin entry's default export (design §3.1): a class that the installer instantiates with the plugin's options.
Everything a plugin can do while it is activated (design §3.2).
Transactional registration (design §3.3.1): the one installation path for built-in plugins, plugins listed in the composition root and (from S8) plugins loaded from a configuration.
A plugin's `package.json`, parsed and checked (design §3.3.2, N11): the package `name` and the registration names it declares under `contributes`.
The options a plugin is constructed with (design §3.1, §4.4): an immutable value object holding a deep, frozen copy of a JSON-like object.

The only implementation of `PluginContext` (design §3.3): registrations go into a staging area and reach the committed registries only through `ExtensionRegistry.commit`, after the installer's checks.
Host entry of the kernel, `@svgframe/kernel/host` (design §3.10, P5a): what only the assembly side (src/) needs to install plugins and build an editor.
File system port used by `read` / `save` (README §4.8, rule D5).
Hands out the ids of imported elements (F13, F14).
Outcome of a successful import: the new document and the warnings raised while building it, in document order.
One read of one file (design §2.1.3, §2.1.4): the `ShapeReader` that shape providers are given, plus the dispatch that chooses a provider per element.
SVG file → new `SvgDocument` plus warnings.

A document → SVG text in the F18 format: XML declaration, 2-space indentation, attributes in `svgAttributes()` order, childless elements self-closed, `& < > "` escaped in attribute values and text, final newline.
Adapter (README §2.8): parses text with `@xmldom/xmldom` and converts the library's DOM into `XmlElement`s, so nothing else depends on the W3C DOM.

The io layer's own XML element, independent of any XML library (Adapter target, README §2.8): local tag name, attributes in document order, child elements, and the character data of the whole subtree.
What an `AttributeHandler.apply` answers (design §2.4.2): the two echoes of the change.
The implementation of `AttributePlanner` (design §2.4.3): asks the handlers, resolves conflicts, and tries the winner out as a snapshot transaction.
The implementation of `PlannedAttributeEdit` (design §2.4.3): snapshots of the target subtree from before and after the handler ran, plus the two echoes obtained then.
Extension point ④ (design §2.4): what setting one attribute means on one kind of shape.
The attribute-handler pipeline as `set` sees it (design §2.4.3), `CommandContext.attributeEdits()`.

The restricted target subtree an `AttributeHandler.apply` works on (design §2.4.2): it can read, and set whitelisted attributes, but has no structural operation at all (no insert, no remove, no container), so a handler cannot change the structure that the snapshots of the `set` transaction cover.
Immutable canvas width × height in px; both must be positive and finite (F2).
Ordered children of a container.
A paint value (`fill`, `stroke`): any non-empty text, no color syntax check (E5, E9).
Composite: a shape that holds child shapes (design §3.5).
Strategy: how a geometry attribute reacts to move and scale, and which values it accepts.
Read-only view of a document (design §3.6.1), what tree decorators and document listeners get and what `SvgSerializer` reads.
The only implementation of `AttributeTarget` (design §2.4.2): one shape of the target subtree of a `set`.
A user-visible, expected failure (bad input, missing id, constraint violation…).
Read-only view of one XML element, handed to shape providers during read-back (design §2.1.4).
A size (width, height, r, rx, ry): unaffected by move, must be ≥ 0 (E4).
Attributes outside the editable whitelist found when reading a file (`transform`, `font-size`, `data-*`…).
The `<reason>` of a contract-breach message such as `plugin failed to activate: <name> (<reason>)` (design §3.3.1, §3.9): the first line of an `Error`'s message, otherwise `String(value)`.
Context of the `CoordinateRole` strategy: one named numeric geometry attribute of a leaf shape (e.g. `width`), stored at full precision (V3).
Character-set rule for ids created from the CLI (convention F16).
Shared implementation of leaf shapes.
Strict number parsing (convention R8) and the single output format (V3) shared by tree, show, command echoes and serialization.

Describes one positional `create` parameter of a shape type: the name shown in usage text, the attribute it sets, whether it may be omitted, and whether a file stores it as element content rather than as an XML attribute.
An attribute change that has been resolved and tried out (design §2.4.3), what `AttributePlanner.plan` answers and `set` keeps.

Composite component: every shape element (leaf or `<g>`) has an id, an optional parent, style attributes and pass-through attributes, and supports the same operations so that commands never ask which concrete class it is.
The committed shape types, read-only plus "build by name" (design §2.1.2).
What can hold child shapes: a `ContainerShape` and the document root `SvgDocument`.

"Build a shape of this type by name" (design §2.1.2, §2.1.5): what a shape provider is given in `create`, so that a composite type can build its parts (for example a `rect` and a `text`) without importing another plugin.
Memento: the attribute state of one shape and, for a container, of all its descendants.
Extension point ①: one shape type (design §2.1.2).
What the kernel offers a shape provider during read-back (design §2.1.4).
Name dispatch #1 (spec §2.1): type name → shape provider.

The static side of a shape class: the class object itself satisfies this interface (static `typeName`, `params`, `create`), so `ShapeRegistry` stores classes directly and the compiler checks each class when it is registered.
Read-only view of a shape (design §3.6.1), what tree decorators, the `handles` of attribute handlers and document listeners get.
Adapter (design §2.1.2): Target `ShapeProvider`, Adaptee `ShapeType` — the static side of a shape class.
`stroke-width`: a full-precision number validated like a size (≥ 0, E4).
The common optional attributes `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, held as an ordered list of property objects; the list order is the serialization and display order (F18, V6).
One optional style attribute of a shape (`fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`).
The document root `<svg>`: canvas size plus top-level shapes.
Value object: where a shape sits in the tree, as (parent container, index).
A horizontal position (x, cx, x1, x2): follows dx, any finite value (E4).
A vertical position (y, cy, y1, y2): follows dy, any finite value (E4).
The §5.2 `show` detail (V6):
Extension point ③ (design §2.3): a tag appended to lines of the structure tree.
The §5.1 structure tree.
The only implementation of `TreeRowView`: a shape line, or the root line when there is no shape.
One line of a `tree` output as a tree decorator sees it (design §2.3.1, §2.3.2): the document root line `svg (800x600)`, or a shape line (the first line of `tree <id>` is a shape line too).
`addto <gid> <id>`: moves an existing shape to the end of a container (E24–E26); the same container is allowed and moves it to the end (E25).
`back <id>`: first among its siblings, i.e. drawn first and at the bottom (E27).
The 19 commands of Phase 1 as a plugin (design §3.3.3).
The static side of `canvas [w] [h]` (README §2.1): one name, two kinds of command.
`create <type> <id> [params…] [in <containerId>]` (spec §3, §4.1).
`delete <id>`: detaches the shape (a container with its whole subtree).
`front <id>`: last among its siblings, i.e. drawn last and on top (E27).
`group <newGid> <id1> <id2>…`: a new `g` takes in existing shapes, which may come from different containers (E16–E19).
`help`: every registered command, grouped by the four categories of spec §3 in `CommandCategory.order()`; registration order within a group (V7).
`init [w] [h]`: a new empty canvas becomes the current document, with no default save path (F5).
`move <id> <dx> <dy>`: translation; a container moves all its descendants.
`read <file.svg>`: the file becomes the current document and its path the default `save` path.
`redo`: redoes the latest undone edit; the output is the same as the command's first run (U6).
`canvas <w> <h>`: changes the canvas size of the current document.
`save [file.svg]`: writes the current document.
`scale <id> <factor>`: every geometry attribute times `factor`, about the origin (E12).
`set <id> <attr> <value>` (§4.1 whitelist, E6–E9; attribute handlers, design §2.4.3).
`canvas` without arguments: shows the canvas size.
`show <id>`: the §5.2 attribute detail of one shape (V6), laid out by `ShapeDetailRenderer`.
`tree [id]`: the §5.1 structure tree of the whole document, or of the subtree rooted at one shape (V4, V5).
`undo`: undoes the latest edit and prints its undo echo.
`ungroup <gid>`: the children take the container's place in its parent, in their order (E20–E23).
Template for `front` / `back` (README §2.6): record the index, move the shape among its siblings, move it back on undo.
The six shape types of Phase 1 as a plugin (design §2.1.1): each class's static side is adapted by `StaticShapeProvider`.
`<circle cx cy r>`.
`<ellipse cx cy rx ry>`.
The `<g>` container.
`<line x1 y1 x2 y2>`.
`<rect x y width height>`.
`<text x y>content</text>`: besides geometry it holds the text content.
Adapter pattern, the Client: `dir` lists the direct children of the working directory, directories first, each group in UTF-16 code-unit order (spec §2.2, design §8.2).

The registered static side of `dir` (design §2.2.1, G11): an instance, not the command class, because it carries the two Targets the Client needs and a static field holding them would be module-level state (L8).
Registers the `dir` command (spec §2.2, design §8.2); it takes no options.
Adapter pattern, the Target's data: one direct child of a directory as the `dir` command sees it, a name and whether it counts as a directory.
Adapter pattern, the Target: the directory access interface the `dir` command (the Client) is written against (spec §2.2 "设计要求", design §8.2).
Adapter pattern, the Adapter: makes Node's file system (the Adaptee: `readdirSync`, `Dirent`, `statSync`) fit the `DirectoryLister` Target.
Adapter pattern, the Adapter for the second Target: the process's current directory (the Adaptee: `process.cwd()`, an absolute path) as a `WorkingDirectory`.
Adapter pattern, a second Target: where the `dir` command (the Client) learns which directory to list.
Counts leaves by kind name in first-seen order, and containers separately (spec §2.1).
`stats`: leaf counts by type in first-seen order, then the totals, on one line (spec §2.1).
Registers the `stats` command (spec §2.1, design §8.1); it takes no options.
The `AttributeHandler` of box (design §2.4.2, §8.3): `set <box> fill` goes to the frame rect, `set <box> label` rewrites the title text.
The `AttributeChange` of `set <box> fill` (design §2.4.2, §2.4.6): `box#n2 fill propagated to n2-rect` / `box#n2 fill restored on n2-rect`.
The `AttributeChange` of `set <box> label` (design §2.4.2, §2.4.6): `box#n2 label updated: "v2"` / `box#n2 label restored: "v1"`.
The plugin entry (design §3.1, §8.3): the `box` shape type with its attribute semantics and tree tag.

The `ShapeProvider` of box (design §2.1.2, §8.3): the `create` parameters, the three ids a box occupies, the template built from a `rect` and a `text` through `ShapeKit`, the creation echo, and read-back of `<g data-kind="box">` with degradation to a plain `g` when the parts are not as expected (decisions X6, X7; ADR-2).
`box` (P1 spec §4.4, design §8.3): the Composite container of the box type, written as `<g data-kind="box">` and holding the frame rect `<id>-rect` and the title text `<id>-label`.
The `TreeDecorator` of box (design §2.3, §8.3): the tag `(box)` on box rows only, so the tree shows `g#n1 (box)`.
The `TreeDecorator` and `DocumentListener` of modified-star (design §2.3, §3.4, §8.4, ADR-3): `*` on rows whose content differs from the last save, read or init point.

The save point of modified-star (design §8.4, ADR-3): an immutable value object holding one fingerprint per shape id and the serialized text of the whole document, as they were at the last `init`, `read` or `save`.
The plugin entry (design §3.1, §8.4): the tree tag `modified-star`.
`FileSystem` on Node's synchronous fs API; the only file allowed to import `node:fs` (rule P1).
Which optional plugins an assembly installs after the built-ins (design §4.3).

What an assembly produced (design §4.1): the editor, and the startup messages — one `error: …` line per optional plugin that failed, in installation order — that the REPL prints after the banner (design §4.5).
`--bare`: the built-in shapes and commands only, the Phase 1 editor (design §4.3, N14).
Way A: the plugins to install, listed in code.
`--config <file>`: way B, the built-ins plus the plugins of the configuration, not the composition root's optional plugins (design §4.3: otherwise a plugin listed in both would be installed twice).

Builds an `Editor` for an assembly profile (design §4.1–§4.3): installs the built-in plugins, then the profile's optional plugins (way A from the composition root, way B through the loader), all through one `PluginInstaller`, and wires the session to the file system.
No argument: way A, every optional plugin of the composition root in its order (design §4.3).
`--only <package>…`: part of way A — the composition root's optional plugins whose package name (the candidate's label) was given, still in the order of `optional()` (design §4.3).
The process must not start: the command line asks for something that cannot be assembled (design §4.3) — a usage error from `CliArguments`, or an `--only` name that is not in the code assembly.
The command line of `svg-editor` (design §4.3): which assembly profile to build.
The read–eval–print loop (README §1.2): prints the banner, then hands every input line unchanged to the `Editor` and writes the lines it returns.
Program entry point (`npm run cli`).
A configuration entry, or the configuration itself, that failed before installation (design §4.5 rows 1–3, 8, 9).
A plugin that was found and imported: it goes through the one installation path (design §4.1).

One entry of an assembly's list of optional plugins, in installation order: either a candidate ready for the installer (`LoadedCandidate`) or a failure already known before installation (`LoadFailure`, e.g. `plugin not found`).
Where a configured module lives (design §4.6, stage 1): its package directory, its parsed `package.json` (the manifest the installer checks) and the absolute path of its entry file (`exports["."]`).

Stage 1 of loading (design §4.6): turns a module string from a plugin configuration into a `LocatedModule` without importing anything, so that "the module does not exist" can be told apart from "the module exists but fails to load" (Node reports both as `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`).

A plugin configuration file such as `plugins.config.json` (way B, design §4.4), read and checked strictly: the top level is an object whose only key is `plugins`, an array of entries (`PluginConfigEntry`).

One item of the `plugins` array of a plugin configuration (design §4.4): the module string exactly as written, whether it is enabled, and its options as a frozen deep copy (`PluginOptions.of`, `{}` when absent).
Way B (design §4.1, §4.6): turns a plugin configuration into the list of optional plugins to install, one `LoadedPlugin` per enabled entry, in array order.

files.responsibility: The short text shown next to a resource in the Explorer, plus its tooltip.
A `vscode.FileType` value, decoded without importing `vscode`.
An element whose start tag has been read but whose end tag has not (yet): one entry of `OutlineTreeBuilder`'s stack.
One element in the outline: everything the host needs to build a `vscode.DocumentSymbol`, already decided here (spec A.2, VA17–VA20).
The structural role of an element in the outline (VA18), decided from the tree alone — no SVG vocabulary:
Builds the outline tree from the tag stream with an explicit stack, so nesting depth costs heap, not call stack.
What a resource is, in the extension's own terms (independent of `vscode.FileType`).
The path part of a resource URI (`Uri.path`: always `/`-separated, never a Windows path), with the naming questions the badge rule needs.
Which URI schemes the extension decorates at all (VA6).
A half-open range `[start, end)` of UTF-16 offsets into a document's text.
Spec A.1: a resource gets the `[]` badge exactly when its name ends in `.svg` (case-insensitive, VA3; hidden `.svg` excluded, VA4) **and** it is a file.
The result of parsing one version of a document: the top-level outline nodes, plus the first syntax error when the text is not well-formed (then the nodes cover only the text before the error, VA16).
Spec A.2's pure logic: text → outline tree with source spans (VA13).
Which documents get the SVG outline (VA14): the `DocumentFilter` content, as plain data so it stays testable without `vscode`.
Turns a raw attribute value, as written between the quotes, into the value a DOM would report (`getAttribute`), so `id="a&b"` displays as `a&b` (VA17).
A complete end tag `</name>`, as produced by `XmlTokenizer`.
A complete start tag `<name attr="…" …>` or empty-element tag `<name …/>`, as produced by `XmlTokenizer`.
The text is not (yet) well-formed at `offset`: an unterminated construct, a malformed tag, a mismatched or stray end tag, or elements still open at the end of the text.
A small XML scanner that reports only what an outline needs: start tags and end tags with their exact source offsets (VA13).
Adapter: the core outline tree (`OutlineNode`, UTF-16 offsets) → VSCode's `DocumentSymbol` tree (`Range` of line/character positions).
The object VSCode calls whenever it needs the outline of an SVG document (Outline view, breadcrumbs, "Go to Symbol in Editor").
The object VSCode calls back for every resource it renders (Explorer rows, editor tabs, …).
Turns file-system events for `*.svg` paths into the `onDidChangeFileDecorations` event (VA7).
Adapter: `workspace.fs.stat(uri).type` (a `vscode.FileType` bit mask) → `ResourceKind`.
